de14_map.topic: The money map: documented funding, employment, investment and appointment edges

claims.text: CNBC (FEC): Thiel gave $15M to the pro-Vance super PAC in the Ohio primary and $15M to the pro-Masters super PAC in the Arizona primary plus $2.5M in October 2022; Vance won, Masters lost to Kelly
Axios 12 Oct 2022: the pro-Masters super PAC is Saving Arizona PAC; Thiel spent $15M in the primary; proposed to cover half of a joint $10M+ commitment with Senate Leadership Fund

CBS (OpenSecrets): Thiel gave $15M to Protect Ohio Values; Per Aspera Policy, a dark-money nonprofit Thiel controlled that does not disclose donors, steered at least $200,000 to it (Kansas City Star, OpenSecrets); Mercer, Uihlein, Lindner families gave hundreds of thousands; Sacks $1M (FEC); Thiel brought Vance to Mar-a-Lago Feb 2021 (NYT); Vance's 2019 Ohio venture firm heavily backed by Thiel

Forbes: Narya Capital (2019) reportedly backed by Thiel, Andreessen and Eric Schmidt (Axios); Vance joined Mithril 2015 per Politico, left 2017; Thiel helped recruit about 10 major donors, Sacks $1M (Politico); Thiel at Aspen 2024 would not donate to Trump

CNN (FEC year-end): Musk spent more than $290M in 2024; about a quarter-billion to America PAC; $11.2M on 31 Dec for 'petition incentives'; $1M giveaways cost more than $50M; $10,000 checks to dozens of state GOP committees

WaPo Nov 2025: Rockbridge Network grew out of a 2019 summit convened by Thiel and Vance near Rockbridge, Ohio; no website or public-facing entity; led by Chris Buskirk; Sacks and Andreessen described as members; Rebekah Mercer attended 2019; affiliated super PAC Turnout for America spent $34.5M in 2024 (FEC); Thiel's earlier funding supported Buskirk's American Greatness; Thiel declined comment

Masters co-wrote Zero to One (Sept 2014) with Thiel from notes on Thiel's 2012 Stanford class; COO of Thiel Capital and president of the Thiel Foundation; resigned both in March 2022 to run; won primary Aug 2022 (~40%), lost to Kelly by 4.9%; lost 2024 House primary to Hamadeh

de14_epstein.topic: Epstein, Valar Ventures and Thiel: what the records show and do not show; Epstein files status

claims.text: NYT: in 2015 and 2016 Epstein put $40M into two funds managed by Valar Ventures, a New York firm co-founded by Thiel, led by Andrew McCormack and James Fitzgerald; worth nearly $170M per a confidential estate analysis and a Valar spokesperson; largest asset still held by the estate; locked up; Valar spokesperson Aaron Curtis: a firm representative met Epstein in 2014 when he was a 'well-known adviser to world leaders, top universities and philanthropic organizations'; hopes distribution can help victims; Thiel spokesperson Jeremiah Hall declined comment

Byline Times from DOJ-released files (no document IDs): 15 Nov 2014 email soliciting $10–20M for Valar; by June 2015 Epstein committed $15M through Southern Trust Company as LP; Valar Global Fund III statements; Feb 2016 Barak email: 'a new Investment Fund owned by Peter Thiel and JE'; Thiel spokesman denied co-ownership and confirmed LP status; June 2017 'super confidential' opportunities; Nov 2018 further solicitation

Jacobin citing EFTA00832976 (DOJ Data Set 9): Epstein in late Feb 2016 proposed meeting Thiel in Europe, on his island or in Saudi Arabia; Thiel: 'Certainly not in Saudi — just think I will avoid the Middle East for the next decade or so'; Epstein emails show efforts to connect Thiel and Barak on at least six occasions

Stanford Daily from DOJ files: meetings 2014 to early 2019 at Epstein's New York home, Thiel's SF office and home (EFTA01027688); Aug 2015 Palo Alto dinner with several CEOs (EFTA00666028); Epstein offered tax advice June 2014 (EFTA02104079); Epstein $40M in Valar (EFTA00591691); considered buying Palantir shares (EFTA00814818); repeated island invitations, Thiel replied 'When are you there?' (EFTA00995535); Epstein called Thiel a 'great friend' to associates (EFTA01618783); Thiel spokesperson told NYT Thiel 'never went to Epstein's Island'

Epstein Files Transparency Act signed 19 Nov 2025 with a 19 Dec deadline; on 21 Jan 2026 Judge Engelmayer declined to appoint a special master, citing lack of jurisdiction while acknowledging 'legitimate concerns'

DOJ released more than 3 million pages, 2,000+ videos and 180,000 images (late January 2026), about 3.5 million pages in total under the law; Blanche: obligations complete once final report submitted and redaction justifications published

DOJ 'Report Under Public Law 119-38' notice dated 21 Aug 2026, Federal Register publication 27 Aug 2026: categories released and withheld, summary of redactions and legal basis, list of government officials and politically exposed persons named
